description:
WHAT: Runs the Fairquery Apify Actor email-validator-mx-disposable: syntax, domain existence, MX/null-MX, disposable, role, free provider, typo suggestion, SPF/DMARC policy, mail provider; final verdict valid | risky | invalid | unknown.
WHEN: Only when MX/DNS matters (can the domain receive mail?), e.g. cleaning lists before a send or verifying a lead's domain; pre-filter with email_check_syntax to avoid paying for obviously bad rows.
WHEN NOT: Offline format, typo, disposable or role checks (free email_check_syntax). Leads that also need sanctions screening: trust_screen_lead (one merged decision). It does not SMTP-probe mailboxes.
COST: Paid, billed to YOUR Apify account via your APIFY_TOKEN: $0.79 per 1,000 emails (+ $0.05 per 1,000 runs). 100 emails ~ $0.08.
RETURNS: Paged "email" rows (verdict valid | risky | invalid | unknown with reasons[]) or "error" rows. Tool errors: APIFY_TOKEN_MISSING, APIFY_TOKEN_INVALID, APIFY_PAYMENT_REQUIRED, APIFY_ACTOR_RUN_FAILED, APIFY_TIMEOUT.
BEHAVIOR: No email is sent; results change only with live DNS. Makes network calls: runs an Apify Actor (DNS/MX lookups) in your account; latency seconds to minutes (300 s timeout).
PARAMETERS: emails: elements may also hold comma/semicolon/newline-separated lists or "Name <addr>" forms; the Actor splits them, trims, and skips case-insensitive duplicates, so you pay once per unique address. The allow* flags only decide whether a condition downgrades the verdict to "risky": the matching reason code (ROLE_ACCOUNT, DISPOSABLE_DOMAIN, FREE_PROVIDER) is reported in reasons[] either way, and they can never turn an "invalid" address (bad syntax, no domain, null MX, no mail server) into "valid". POSSIBLE_TYPO and IMPLICIT_MX_ONLY always make it "risky" regardless of flags. Typical presets: B2B lead list = allowFreeProviders false + allowRoleAccounts false; consumer signups = defaults. checkSpfDmarc only adds has_spf / has_dmarc / dmarc_policy fields; it never changes the verdict or the price. limit/offset only page the returned rows: every call validates and bills the whole list again (also when only offset changes), so set limit (max 1000) to cover all rows instead of paging.
EXAMPLE: {"emails":["john@stripe.com"]} -> verdict "valid", has_mx true, mail_provider "Google Workspace / Gmail".

allowDisposable.description: Optional boolean, default false = disposable/temporary-inbox domains (mailinator.com, ...) get verdict "risky"; true stops penalising them

allowFreeProviders.description: Optional boolean, default true. false downgrades free webmail (gmail.com, outlook.com, yahoo.com, ...) to "risky"; recommended for B2B lead lists

allowRoleAccounts.description: Optional boolean, default true. false downgrades role mailboxes (info@, sales@, support@, ...) to verdict "risky"

checkSpfDmarc.description: Optional boolean, default true. true adds has_spf, has_dmarc and dmarc_policy (none|quarantine|reject) per domain; false skips those DNS lookups. Verdict and price are unaffected

emails.description: Required. 1-10000 strings, 1-320 chars each, one address per element; bare "jane@acme.com", "Jane <jane@acme.com>" and "mailto:jane@acme.com" forms accepted. Example: ["jane@acme.com","bob@gmial.com"]

limit.description: Optional page size: items to return, integer 1-1000 (default 100). Example: 50

offset.description: Optional zero-based number of items to skip, integer 0-1000000 (default 0); pass nextOffset from the previous response, e.g. 100

name: email_validate_deliverability

count.description: Number of items in this page

hasMore.description: True if more items exist after this page

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, or null

offset.description: Offset of the first item in this page

title: Validate email deliverability: MX, SPF, DMARC (paid)
